description:
A global bank standing up its India technology and operations centre has reached a size where the centre needs its own governance rhythm rather than borrowing the parent entity's, and Flexiple, a managed marketplace placing specialist talent inside global companies' India teams, has been asked to help hire the person who will build it.
 



**Governance for a centre finding its own footing** 




 You would support the India centre's local board and governance committees end to end: preparing agendas and board packs, drafting minutes and resolutions, maintaining statutory registers, and coordinating the filings the centre owes to the Registrar of Companies and other authorities. You would also track compliance with the Companies Act and applicable Reserve Bank of India governance requirements for the centre's legal entity, and work with the global governance team to make sure local reporting lines up with what the parent entity expects.
 



**Where the gaps currently sit** 



* Board pack preparation is done ad hoc by whoever has time, with no fixed template or timeline
* Statutory registers have not been consistently updated as the centre has grown
* There is no single person accountable for the centre's Companies Act compliance calendar



**The profile we are hiring for** 



* 3 to 7 years in corporate governance or company secretarial work, ideally at a bank, financial\-services company, or large corporate
* A Company Secretary qualification, or an LLB with hands\-on governance and secretarial experience
* Working knowledge of Companies Act requirements and ROC filing processes
* Comfort setting up process where none currently exists, and working with both local and global stakeholders



 Location: Mumbai, Chennai, Hyderabad — hybrid, based alongside the centre's leadership and legal team
 



 Expect an HR screening, a working round on a governance\-calendar exercise, and a closing round with centre leadership.
 



 Flexiple keeps this application active for this role and future governance openings that fit your background.

 Compliance and audit findings closed on time; vulnerability remediation
   

  

 performance against the agreed SLAs (critical / high); security awareness results (training completion rate, phishing simulation click and report rates); timeliness and quality of the compliance evidence, metrics and reporting.
   

  

**Required**

* At least 8 years of experience in IT or cyber security, with hands\-on exposure to compliance, audit support and reporting (a GRC or internal audit background is an advantage)

description:

Mumbai, MH, IN

JOB PURPOSE
  
Seeking a proactive legal professional with 4\-7 years' experience in Legal Metrology and Contracts, preferably in FMCG/Manufacturing/Retail. The candidate must have hands\-on experience in Legal Metrology laws and Packaged Commodities Regulations. Responsibilities include ensuring label compliance, artwork and label approvals, stakeholder communication, legal training, and compliance audits under the Legal Metrology Act and allied rules. Candidate should have knowledge on drafting and negotiating contracts.
  
  

Primary Responsibilities
  
  

Safeguard the Company's interests by providing legal support on commercial and business transactions, drafting and negotiating contracts, minimizing legal and commercial risks, ensuring regulatory compliance, and supporting dispute management. The role will primarily focus on contract management while demonstrating willingness to support Legal Metrology compliance initiatives as required.
  
  

BUSINESS RESPONSIBILITY AREAS
  
1\. Contract Drafting \& Negotiation
  
* Draft, review, negotiate and finalize a wide range of commercial contracts, including procurement agreements, service agreements, NDAs, marketing agreements, logistics contracts, consultancy agreements, amendments and other business\-related documents.
* Identify legal, commercial and operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
* Standardize contract templates and assist in developing contracting playbooks.
* Provide legal support during negotiations with customers, vendors, service providers and other stakeholders.


2\. Legal Advisory \& Risk Management
  
* Advise business teams on contractual rights, obligations, liabilities, indemnities, warranties, limitation of liability and dispute resolution mechanisms.
* Ensure business transactions comply with applicable laws, company policies and internal approval frameworks.
* Conduct legal due diligence and support evaluation of strategic business projects.


3\. Contract Governance \& Compliance
  
* Monitor contract lifecycle management, including execution, amendments, renewals and closures.
* Maintain contract repositories and ensure proper record keeping and document management.
* Support periodic audits and compliance reviews relating to contractual obligations.


4\. Dispute \& Litigation Support
  
* Assist in managing contractual disputes, claims, legal notices and commercial disagreements arising from business transactions.
* Support assessment of legal risks, contractual exposure and dispute resolution strategies to safeguard the Company's interests.
* Coordinate with external counsel, business teams and internal stakeholders for litigation, arbitration, mediation and other dispute resolution proceedings.
* Assist in the preparation, review and management of legal notices, replies, pleadings, legal opinions, claim assessments and settlement documentation.
* Monitor ongoing litigation and dispute matters, maintain case records and ensure timely submission of required documents and information.
* Support preservation of evidence, fact\-finding exercises and internal investigations relating to contractual and commercial disputes.
* Work closely with business teams to identify contentious issues at an early stage and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.
* Assist in enforcing contractual rights, remedies and dispute resolution mechanisms under various commercial agreements.
* Provide legal support in negotiating and documenting settlements, compromise arrangements and dispute closure mechanisms.
* Derive learnings from disputes and claims to strengthen contracting practices, risk allocation provisions and contract governance frameworks.
* Assist in managing contentious matters, high\-stake disputes, strategic litigation and business\-critical legal issues having significant financial, operational, regulatory or reputational impact on the Company.
* Support preparation of management updates, litigation trackers and risk reports for senior leadership and key stakeholders.


5\. Stakeholder Management \& Training
  
* Partner with Sales, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing and other business functions to provide timely legal support.
* Conduct training sessions and awareness programs on contracts, legal risks and governance requirements.


6\. Regulatory Support
  
* Track legal and regulatory developments impacting commercial contracts and business operations.
* Support implementation of legal compliance initiatives across the organization.


7\. Legal Metrology (Developmental Exposure)
  
* Demonstrate an interest and willingness to learn and support Legal Metrology compliance matters, including product labelling and packaging requirements under the Legal Metrology framework.

title: Legal Ops Specialist
description:
**Overview**
**About the Role**
 We are seeking a detail\-oriented and highly organized
 **Legal Operations Specialist** 
 to support the Legal Department in managing legal operations, technology, spend, matter management, outside counsel processes, and reporting.
   

  

 The successful candidate will work closely with Legal, Finance, Procurement, business stakeholders, and external law firms to ensure efficient and accurate management of legal matters and legal spend. This role will also support the administration and continuous improvement of legal technology platforms and operational processes.
   

  

**Key Responsibilities** 
**1\. Legal eBilling \& Legal Spend Management**
* Manage day\-to\-day administration of the Legal Department's electronic billing and legal spend management processes.
* Review and validate outside counsel invoices for compliance with billing guidelines, negotiated rates, billing arrangements, and applicable policies.
* Monitor invoice submissions, approvals, rejections, adjustments, and payment status.
* Support implementation and maintenance of automated invoice validation and auto\-rejection rules.
* Identify billing discrepancies, duplicate invoices, rate issues, timekeeper exceptions, and other billing violations.
* Work with law firms to resolve invoice and billing issues.
* Monitor outside counsel spend against budgets and approved matter estimates.
* Support development of cost\-saving initiatives and identify opportunities to improve legal spend efficiency.


**2\. Matter Management**
* Maintain accurate and complete legal matter records within the Legal Department's matter management system.
* Support matter opening, updates, closures, categorization, and data quality activities.
* Ensure matters are appropriately tagged by region, legal lead, matter type, agreement type, business function, and other required fields.
* Conduct periodic data cleansing and quality reviews of matter management data.
* Support matter intake and triage processes and ensure requests are routed to the appropriate Legal team member.
* Monitor aging and inactive matters and coordinate with Legal stakeholders for appropriate closure or follow\-up.


**3\. Legal Accruals \& Forecasting**
* Coordinate monthly, quarterly, and year\-end legal accrual processes with Legal, Finance, and external counsel.
* Collect and validate accrual estimates from law firms and internal Legal stakeholders.
* Track actual spend against accruals and identify significant variances.
* Support forecasting of legal spend and provide analysis of budget versus actual expenditure.
* Prepare accrual reports and supporting information for Finance and Legal leadership.

description:

 Razorpay powers millions of businesses with a smarter, scalable stack that goes beyond transactions to help them truly build and grow.
   

  

 From building AI\-native agentic payments, to AI\-assisted fraud detection and real\-time risk intelligence to automated reconciliation, smart payouts, and predictive financial insights, we are embedding intelligence across our stack to make money movement faster, safer, and more efficient. In close collaboration with ecosystem partners \- including banks, networks, regulators \- we are pioneering industry\-first solutions that are shaping the next era of fintech
   

  

 Across India, Singapore and Malaysia, our products span everything from seamless checkouts to payroll automation \- powering a fintech ecosystem that’s redefining how money moves across Asia.
   

  

 Today, that ecosystem supports everyone from early\-stage startups to some of India’s largest enterprises, enabling them to accept, process, and disburse payments at scale while expanding into new ways of managing money more efficiently.
   

  

 Our scale speaks volumes: Razorpay processes $180\+ billion in annualized transactions, powering leading businesses like Airbnb, Facebook, WhatsApp, Airtel, CRED, BookmyShow, Zomato, Swiggy, Lenskart, Mirae Asset Capital markets, Indian Oil, National Pension Scheme \- and over 100 of India’s unicorns. With strong roots in India and growing operations in Southeast Asia, we are shaping the next chapter of financial technology across the region.
   

  

 We are backed by global investors including GIC, Peak XV Partners (formerly Sequoia Capital India \& SEA), Tiger Global, Ribbit Capital, Matrix Partners, MasterCard, and Salesforce Ventures, having raised over $740 million to date. Strategic acquisitions \- including Ezetap (POS and offline payments), Curlec (Malaysia expansion), BillMe (digital invoicing), and POP (rewards\-first UPI) \- along with earlier moves in fraud prevention, payroll, and lending, have further strengthened our platform and widened our footprint across Asia.
   

  

 But what truly sets Razorpay apart is our culture. At Razorpay, ownership is our oxygen \- you own what you build, with no micromanagement or red tape, just the runway to make your ideas fly. Learning is a lifestyle \- if you’re curious, you’ll feel at home here. People \> Pedigree \- we hire for attitude, hustle, and hunger more than degrees. Transparency thrives over titles \- this is where interns question CXOs and CXOs say “thank you.” Guided by our values of Customer First, Autonomy \& Ownership, Agility with Integrity, Transparency, Challenging the status quo and a strong belief that Razorpay grows with Razors, you’ll be part of a 3000\+ strong team building not just products, but the financial infrastructure of the future.

**About The Role**
 Zeta is seeking a Associate Director – Legal to serve as a strategic advisor within its legal team, supporting the company’s banking, payments, and technology business as it scales across India, the US, the UK, and other global markets.
   

  

 This is a high\-impact, product\-facing role for a seasoned banking and finance lawyer who can operate at the intersection of financial services regulation and cutting\-edge technology, ensuring Zeta’s products, partnerships, and client programs are designed and delivered in a manner that is legally sound and regulator\-ready. Reporting into Zeta’s India legal leadership and partnering closely with Product, Compliance, and Risk teams, the role carries significant autonomy and visibility — requiring an individual who can independently own matters end to end, negotiate directly with banks, NBFCs, and technology partners, run and manage a team of capable lawyers, and help shape the legal function of a fast\-growing, high\-growth fintech at the core of India’s digital banking transformation.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
**Product and platform legal support**
* Deliver day\-to\-day legal counsel across Zeta’s banking technology stack, covering card issuance, transaction processing, lending and loan management, core account and ledger functionality, and Digital Credit\-as\-a\-Service and Credit Line on UPI (CLOU), BNPL, and EMI\-conversion products.
* Advise product and engineering teams on the regulatory implications of platform features, including card management, real\-time authorization and settlement, digital lending, account lifecycle management, instrument lifecycle management (physical and virtual cards, tokens, and QR), transaction switching, and fraud and dispute management.


**Contract drafting, review, and negotiation**
* Draft, review, and negotiate agreements with banks, financial institutions, card networks, and technology partners, including platform licensing, SaaS and managed\-services arrangements, program\-management agreements, and BIN or balance\-sheet sponsorship deals underpinning Banking\-as\-a\-Service and embedded banking offerings.
* Structure co\-brand, affinity, and fintech partnership arrangements, and draft and negotiate credit card, debit card, prepaid instrument, and co\-branded card program agreements spanning retail, commercial, private\-label, and secured card products.
* Structure and paper credit lines, BNPL, and loan\-installment features and related payment and settlement arrangements, and negotiate digital lending, co\-lending, and lending service provider (LSP) agreements.
* Draft, negotiate, and manage fintech partnership, third\-party vendor, and platform licensing agreements, allocating responsibility, liability, and data\-handling obligations across Zeta, its clients, and its partners.


**Regulatory advisory**
* Advise on RBI guidelines including the Digital Lending Directions, Credit Card and Debit Card Issuance and Conduct Directions, and Master Direction on Outsourcing of IT Services; NPCI regulations governing UPI and RuPay; and PPI rules under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act — tracking evolving developments and assessing their impact on Zeta’s products and programs.
* Advise on card\-network rules, grievance redressal frameworks, and partner bank agreement requirements for card and payments programs.
* Advise on data privacy, cybersecurity, and data\-localization requirements under the DPDP Act and IT Act, and on legal considerations relevant to maintaining SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications.
* Provide legal input on regulatory filings, regulator queries and inspections, and legal risk assessments for new products and partnerships, and support the development of internal legal playbooks and templates.


**Broader legal support**
* While anchored in banking and finance law, comfortable providing practical legal support across other areas as they arise for a fast\-growing technology business, including corporate, commercial, employment, and technology or intellectual property matters.


**Skills**
* Regulatory and commercial acumen: Commercially minded, pragmatic; translates complex regulation into clear, actionable guidance for non\-legal stakeholders.
* Stakeholder management and communication: Strong communication and negotiation skills, sound and independent judgment, ability to counsel senior management strategically.
* Execution and prioritization: Highly organized and detail\-oriented; manages multiple matters simultaneously in a fast\-paced, high\-growth setting; ability to leverage AI for legal work highly preferred.
* Team leadership and people management: Ability to lead and manage a team effectively.
* Ownership and adaptability: Proactive self\-starter, energized by ambiguity, comfortable in unfamiliar areas of law, takes ownership of outcomes, thrives in a collaborative, product\-driven culture at the frontier of banking and fintech.


**Experience And Qualification**
* LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognized institution; qualified to practice law in India. LLM is a plus.
* 9–12 years of post\-qualification experience as a banking and finance lawyer, gained in a top tier law firm.
* H ands\-on expertise across digital lending, credit and debit cards, prepaid and co\-branded card programs, payments, and fintech regulation.
* Contract drafting \& negotiation: Strong contract drafting, review, and negotiation skills across commercial, technology, and financial\-services agreements.
* Working command of RBI, NPCI, and PPI frameworks.
* Experience advising on software license, SaaS, IT services, and IP licensing matters; f amiliarity with Banking\-as\-a\-Service; c ross\-border regulatory exposure.
* Proven experience leading and managing a team, including handling administrative responsibilities alongside substantive legal work.

title: Legal Manager
description:
**Legal Manager – Land \& Title \| 5–9 Years** 




**MSR Infraa \| Bengaluru** 




 We are looking for a
 **Legal Manager – Land \& Title** 
 who can independently examine incoming land opportunities, build the title file, identify deal\-breakers and give the Managing Director a clear
 **YES / NO / CONDITIONAL** 
 recommendation — quickly and with evidence.
 



 This is not a conventional documentation or contract\-management role.
 



 You will sit close to the
 **land acquisition and development decision\-making process** 
 , with direct responsibility for Karnataka land due diligence.
 



**What You Will Own** 




**1\. First\-Hand Land Due Diligence** 




 Every incoming land parcel, JDA proposal or outright purchase comes to you first.
 



 You will:
 


* Review title and revenue documents.
* Trace the revenue and ownership chain.
* Identify legal and documentary gaps.
* Flag deal\-breakers and potential risks.
* Prepare a clear internal title opinion note.
* Give the MD a practical
 **YES / NO / CONDITIONAL** 
 recommendation.



**Target turnaround: 7–10 working days per parcel.** 




 External senior counsel steps in
 **after your internal file is substantially clean.** 








  





**2\. Build the Complete Title File** 




 You should know exactly
 **what to collect, where to obtain it and in what sequence.** 




 Your work will include:
 


* Pahani / RTC extracts
* Mutation Register (MR)
* Akarband
* 11E Sketch
* Section 4(1\) Tippani
* Index of Lands
* 10(1\) Extract
* 30\-year Encumbrance Certificates
* Mother deed tracing
* Survey records
* Conversion orders
* Revenue and registration records



 You will own the
 **collection, sequencing, indexing and completeness** 
 of the land title file.
 







  





**3\. Construct the Mother Deed Chain** 




 You should be comfortable going deep into the ownership history of a property.
 



 Trace and analyse:
 



**Sale Deeds → Gift Deeds → Partition Deeds → Family Arrangements → Inheritance → Court Orders / Decrees → Current Ownership** 




 Your job is to identify:
 


* Breaks in the title chain
* Unregistered transfers
* Missing documents
* Inconsistent ownership records
* Unexplained gaps
* Potentially defective transactions



**A clean title chain should be understandable on one table — not buried across 200 pages of documents.** 








  





**4\. Karnataka Land Law – This Is Critical** 




 You should be able to independently identify Karnataka\-specific risks involving:
 


* **PTCL Act**
* **Inam Abolition history**
* **Karnataka Land Reforms Act – Sections 79A / 79B**
* **Section 63 and conversion status**
* Old tenancy entries in Pahani
* Land ceiling
* Gramathana vs. revenue land
* BBMP / BDA / BMRDA jurisdiction
* Mutation and survey issues
* Phodi / re\-survey matters



**You should see the trap before the transaction gets into it.** 








  





**5\. Revenue \& Registry Liaison** 




 This is a hands\-on role.
 



 You should have direct experience working with:
 


* Tahsildar Office
* Sub\-Registrar Office
* Survey Department
* Assistant Commissioner
* Deputy Commissioner Office



 You should understand
 **which authority issues which document, what the practical turnaround is, and how to move a stuck file forward.** 




 We are looking for someone who has
 **personally handled these processes** 
 , not someone who has only instructed junior staff to do them.
 







  





**6\. Existing Project Title Files** 




 You will maintain and close documentation gaps for our ongoing projects and upcoming projects.
 



 When a bank, buyer, auditor or internal team asks for a document, you should be able to retrieve it quickly.
 



**Our expectation: any critical title document should be retrievable within 24 hours.** 








  





**7\. Buyer Documentation** 




 Approximately
 **30% of your role** 
 will involve project\-level legal documentation, including:
 


* Agreements of Sale
* Construction Agreements
* Sale Deeds
* Tripartite Agreements with home\-loan banks
* NOCs
* Cancellations
* Nomination changes







  





**8\. K\-RERA Execution** 




 You will support the execution and ongoing compliance process, including:
 


* Quarterly filings
* Amendment tracking
* Agent registrations
* Documentation and records



 Major drafting and registrations will continue to be supported by external counsel.
 







  





**What You Will NOT Own** 




 We have deliberately defined this role.
 



**You will not be responsible for:** 



* ❌ Issuing formal bank title opinions — external senior counsel will do this.
* ❌ Drafting major K\-RERA registration applications — external counsel handles this.
* ❌ Leading complex land litigation — external counsel leads; you manage facts and timelines.
* ❌ Tax, GST, stamp duty strategy — handled by our CA firm.
* ❌ Chasing building plan approvals — handled by the approvals consultant.



**Your job is to make the land transaction legally clear enough for the business to make an informed decision.** 








  





**Must\-Have Experience** 




**Qualification** 



* LLB from a recognised Indian university.
* Bar Council enrolment is preferred, but not mandatory.



**Experience** 



* **5–9 years PQE.**
* Minimum
 **4 years of hands\-on Karnataka land due diligence** 
 .
* Experience in one or more of the following environments:
* Bengaluru real estate developer's land/legal team
* Property law firm handling title opinions
* Bank\-panel title\-search practice with developer clients



**Technical Knowledge** 




 You should be able to independently read and interpret:
 


* Pahani / RTC
* Mutation Register
* Akarband
* 11E Sketch
* Section 4(1\) Tippani
* Phodi / Podi records
* Revenue records



 You should have working knowledge of:
 


* Karnataka Land Revenue Act
* Karnataka Land Reforms Act
* Sections 79A / 79B
* Section 63
* PTCL Act
* Inam Abolition Acts
* Karnataka Stamp Act
* Registration Act



**One Non\-Negotiable** 




**Kannada reading is required.** 




 Original Karnataka revenue records are frequently in Kannada. We need someone who can read and interpret them directly without depending on a translator for routine diligence.
 







  





**We Would Particularly Value** 



* Experience drafting and negotiating
 **Joint Development Agreements (JDAs)** 
 .
* Experience with Gramathana / revenue\-site / conversion disputes.
* Record\-of\-rights rectification and mutation corrections.
* Phodi / re\-survey issues.
* Land aggregation involving
 **4–6\+ acres and multiple landowners** 
 .
* Experience with land in Bengaluru's growth corridors and peripheral zones such as
 **Jakkur, Thanisandra, Yelahanka, Hennur, Doddaballapur Road, Sarjapur and Whitefield periphery.**







  





**What Success Looks Like** 




 Within your first year, we want to see a land legal function where:
 



**Every incoming parcel is screened systematically.** 




**Deal\-breakers are identified early.** 




**Title files are complete and structured.** 




**The MD gets a clear commercial legal view — not a 100\-page document dump.** 




**External counsel spends time validating and resolving the important issues, rather than discovering basic gaps.** 




**Land acquisition decisions become faster, better documented and significantly more predictable.** 








  





**If You Can Look at a Land File and Tell Us What Can Kill the Deal — We Want to Meet You.** 




**Role:** 
 Legal Manager – Land \& Title
 



**Experience:** 
 5–9 Years
 



**Location:** 
 Bengaluru
 



**Industry:** 
 Real Estate / Land Acquisition
 



**Focus:** 
 Karnataka Land Due Diligence \& Title
 



**Apply with your CV and a brief note highlighting your experience in Karnataka land title diligence.** 




*Shortlisted candidates may be asked to share a sanitised sample of an internal title opinion note.*

title: Investigating Officer
description:
**Job Purpose** 




 As an Investigation Team member, the candidate will play a pivotal role in conducting investigation globally for thorough and comprehensive investigations into various matters, such as corporate fraud, misconduct, compliance violations, security breaches, or other incidents. The candidate will be responsible for overseeing all aspects of the investigation process, ensuring compliance with legal and ethical standards, and delivering actionable findings and recommendations to senior management or relevant stakeholders.
 



  





 The Investigation Team Lead plays a crucial role in safeguarding the organization's reputation, ensuring compliance, and mitigating risks through effective and ethical investigations. This role demands a leader who can balance legal, ethical, and organizational considerations while leading a dedicated team.
 



  





**Key Accountabilities** 




  





**Planning \& Handling Investigations** 



1. Carry out end\-to\-end investigations by ensuring that all prescribed investigative / operating methodologies for the various types of investigations are adhered to and by conducting proper planning on all investigations.
2. Obtain all relevant evidence related to an investigation. Scrutinize / analyse this evidence and make meaningful observations / conclusions regarding the findings and make appropriate recommendations.
3. Ensure that witnesses / suspects and victims are interviewed and where necessary obtain written statements.
4. Compile investigation reports as per the prescribed operating methodology, containing the findings of investigations.
5. Ensure that each investigation has an accurate, value\- adding conclusion for the type of investigation conducted.
6. Make meaningful recommendations as per the type of investigation. This will include, but not limited to, system / people / process failures or internal and external threats.
7. Assist reporting manager/ HoD and other team (e.g. HR) with relevant findings / documentation for use in disciplinary processes.
8. Ensure that each investigation is concluded within the prescribed and acceptable time limit for the particular type of investigation.
9. Inform management of any suggestions or proposals to enhance investigative methodology / operating procedure.
10. Collect timely intelligence to avert fraud and Security incidences



  





**Team Leadership** 



1. Supervise, mentor, and provide guidance to a team of investigators.
2. Foster a collaborative and productive work environment
3. Assign and prioritize investigation tasks based on urgency and importance.



  





**Interviews and Interrogations** 



1. Conduct interviews with relevant individuals, both employees and external parties.
2. Maintain objectivity and professionalism during interviews.
3. Document findings accurately and ethically.



  





**Case Management** 



1. To maintain case files and central investigations database to operational standards.
2. To attend progress meetings with HoD and concerned management teams.
3. Ensure credible information is provided for MIs produced by Investigation team.
4. Prepare and submit whistle\-blowing reports to the Head of Department. This will also include summary slides to be presented in other management forums like Audit Committee.
5. Support HR and Risk management teams in Fraud Awareness, training and sensitization Campaigns



  





**Risk Identification and Awareness** 



1. Ensure that all risks and/or emerging risks, which are identified during an investigation / interaction with stakeholders, are escalated to line management upon discovery.
2. Identify high\-risk business units and were requested to do so, participate in awareness initiatives.



  





**Stakeholder Management** 



1. Develop and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders to build synergies and teamwork.
2. Actively interact with counterparts in the industry to gain understanding of threats and risks and to share important information on current frauds and fraudsters involved.
3. Any other duty as may be assigned Head of security \& Investigations.



  





**Ideal Job Specifications** 



1. Chartered Accountant, MBA (in Finance and Risk Management)
2. Hold a professional qualification in a relevant field such as CFE.
3. Minimum 5\-10 years of professional experience with investigatory procedures and practice.
4. Relevant certifications (e.g., Certified Fraud Examiner, Certified Professional Investigator) is a plus.
5. Preferred experience in Pharma or Big 4 (Investigation) or any other industry is preferred.
6. Experience in handling Hot\-line
7. Expertise in investigation technique, particularly where conduct involve criminal implications that could result in prosecution before local courts.
8. Strong analytical and critical\-thinking skills.
9. Leadership and team management skills
10. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

 Our IoT\-driven platform and smart electric vehicles are helping cities reduce traffic congestion and carbon emissions while empowering millions with affordable and reliable transportation.
 



 Backed by industry giants like Bajaj Auto and Magna International, Yulu operates at the intersection of mobility, technology, and sustainability. Our mission is to reduce congestion, cut emissions, and transform how India moves — one ride at a time.
 



 With millions of rides completed, thousands of EVs on the road, and a rapidly expanding footprint, we’re not just building EVs — we’re building the future of urban mobility in India.
 



 🔗 Learn more: www.yulu.bike
 



  





**Role Summary** 




 Yulu is looking for a
 **Regional Lead \- South** 
 to join its Public Policy team. This is a high\-ownership role for someone who can take charge of a critical, high\-priority policy charter spanning
 **Maharashtra and Karnataka** 
 , working closely with the Head of Public Policy to ensure seamless execution on the ground.
 



  





 Beyond the state charter, you will also own a core, organisation\-wide work stream focused on
 **state engagements,** 
 including but not limited to building and deepening relationships across the mobility, labour, and gig\-economy ecosystem to drive long\-term partnerships for Yulu. This role sits at the intersection of policy design, stakeholder management, and cross\-functional execution, and is ideal for someone who thrives on ambiguity and enjoys building structure where none exists yet.

* **Own State Policy Charters:** 
 Take end\-to\-end ownership of Yulu's policy priorities in Maharashtra and Karnataka, working closely with the Head of Public Policy to translate strategy into on\-ground execution.
* **Drive State \& Ecosystem Engagement:** 
 Lead a dedicated charter for state\-level engagement, including building relationships across the mobility, labour, and gig\-economy landscape to create long\-term, durable partnerships for Yulu.
* **Work Across Teams:** 
 Partner with Communications, Legal, Operations, and the central policy function on a regular basis, making sure regional policy priorities stay tied to what the business is trying to achieve.
* **Regulatory Expertise:** 
 Keep a close eye on how relevant laws and regulations are shifting, turn that into whitepapers and briefing notes, and be the person leadership turns to for a read on where things stand.

 Assess policy documents, produce sharp knowledge collaterals, and lead stakeholder meetings with government bodies, industry forums, and labour representatives.

 Think and produce outputs independently, balancing high\-level policy design with day\-to\-day operational alignment.

 6–7 years of professional experience in public policy, corporate affairs, government relations, or strategic advocacy.

 Proven track record of engaging with key government stakeholders from a larger\-organisation perspective, not just a transactional or issue\-by\-issue lens.

 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to synthesise complex legal or operational issues into compelling narratives for external government stakeholders.

**Preferred Qualifications** 



* Master's degree or advanced qualification in Public Policy, Business Administration (MBA), Law (LL.B/LL.M), or International Relations.
* Deep familiarity with transport regulations, evolving labour ecosystem, and digital economy frameworks.
* Existing relationships with central ministries, central labour unions, national think tanks, or state\-level transport departments.
* Prior experience within the
 **mobility or transport sector** 
 is a strong plus.
* A self\-motivated individual who thrives in ambiguity and can comfortably pivot between high\-level policy design and on\-the\-ground operational alignment.

title: Independent Director
description:
**Operating reality** 

  





 The company coordinates the movement and clearance of customer goods through carriers, gateways, overseas agents, customs\-facing processes and inland service providers. It may advance duties, freight, storage or other charges and later recover them from customers. The enterprise therefore manages documents, instructions, client money, credit, sanctions exposure and time\-critical handoffs without owning every part of the physical journey.
 



 As part of a large unlisted corporate house, the business is formalising governance for sustained international growth. Gross billings can obscure thin collected contribution, unrecovered pass\-through costs, agent balances, demurrage disputes and contingent liability. The Board seeks an Independent Director who can clarify where the company acts as principal, agent, adviser, custodian or payer—and ensure its controls follow the substance of each role.
 



  





**Independent Director remit** 




  





 The appointee will bring rigorous oversight to trade compliance, customs conduct, document integrity, sanctions screening, client funds, overseas agents, shipment profitability, cyber resilience, claims, credit and acquisitions. The Director must be prepared to examine transaction files and exception evidence, not only revenue and shipment counts.
 



  





**Eleven governance priorities** 




  




1. Role clarity in each service.
 
 Define contractual and actual responsibility for booking, documentation, classification, valuation support, duty funding, insurance, custody, subcontracting and delivery. Accounting and liability should follow the real role.
2. Trade and sanctions compliance.
 
 Govern customer, counterparty, goods, route, vessel or conveyance, destination, end\-use and payment screening. Escalation should address ambiguity and attempted circumvention, not only exact database matches.
3. Customs\-facing integrity.
 
 Protect classification, valuation information, origin documents, licences, declarations, inspection handling and record retention. No employee or intermediary may promise outcomes through improper influence.
4. Document and instruction authenticity.
 
 Review authorised customer contacts, change verification, bills and certificates, release instructions, account changes and high\-risk amendments. Email urgency should not override validation.
5. Client\-money protection.
 
 Establish clear ownership, approved accounts, funding evidence, reconciliation, release, unused balance return and prohibition on using one customer's funds for another obligation.
6. Complete shipment economics.
 
 Capture carrier cost, pass\-through charges, agent fees, credit, storage, demurrage, detention, claims, correction effort and receivable days. Gross billing and booked margin should be reconciled to cash realised.
7. Overseas\-agent governance.
 
 Conduct ownership, competence, sanctions, financial, data\-security and conduct diligence. Maintain usable audit, document\-return, incident and transition rights with alternatives for critical locations.
8. Credit and exposure limits.
 
 Aggregate customer exposure across freight, duties, advances, disputes and guarantees. Overrides must be independently approved and immediately visible when ageing or shipment risk deteriorates.
9. Cargo and claims governance.
 
 Define custody points, condition evidence, survey, notification, recovery, insurer coordination and lessons from recurring loss. Claims should not remain outside contract profitability.
10. Cyber and business continuity.
 
 Test fraudulent instruction, account takeover, carrier or gateway outage, document\-system compromise, ransomware, unavailable agents and sudden route closure. Manual processing must preserve authorisation and audit trails.
11. Acquisition and branch control.
 
 Diligence licences, agent balances, customer advances, contingent customs matters, conduct history, claims, systems and owner dependence. Minimum controls must precede revenue synergies.



  





**Decisions reserved for deeper Board challenge** 




  





 The Director will scrutinise entry into new jurisdictions, major customer credit, duty\-funding models, acquisitions, agency partnerships, guarantees, technology changes, controlled\-cargo categories, claims settlements and any arrangement that materially expands principal liability.
 



 Country or gateway expansion should state local legal responsibilities, agent dependence, settlement flows, data handling, compliance competence, working capital and exit options. A high\-volume customer must be assessed on collected contribution and total exposure, not strategic prestige.
 



  





**Audit Committee dashboard** 




  





 The Board should receive gross and net revenue; collected contribution; unreconciled client funds; duty and freight advances; receivable ageing; disputed pass\-through costs; demurrage and detention; agent balances; screening alerts; customs queries; document corrections; cargo claims; cyber incidents; credit overrides; branch exceptions; acquisition remediation; and downside liquidity excluding client money.
 



 Internal audit should trace selected shipments from quote and customer instruction through booking, documentation, screening, clearance, agent settlement, invoice and collection. It should reperformance\-test bank\-detail changes, client\-fund reconciliation, agent due diligence, sanctions escalation, credit overrides and revenue presentation.
 



  





**Candidate credentials** 




  





 Candidates should have at least 25 years of senior leadership across logistics, freight forwarding, shipping, customs, trade finance, banking operations, compliance, audit, finance or multinational service governance. Suitable experience may come from a CEO, CFO, COO, trade\-compliance head, risk officer, gateway leader, Audit Committee Chair or executive responsible for a global agent network.
 



 The candidate must understand transaction\-level risk, cross\-border conduct and working\-capital economics. Experience with client money, sanctions, customs processes, acquisitions, international partners or large family\-controlled corporate houses will be useful.
 



  





**Independence requirements** 




  





 Active inclusion in the
 
 IICA Independent Directors Databank is mandatory
 
 . The candidate must meet an enhanced independence standard appropriate to a large unlisted company. Interests involving promoter entities, customers, carriers, ports or airports, customs intermediaries, overseas agents, banks, insurers, technology vendors, auditors or acquisition targets must be disclosed.
 



 The role may not be used to steer cargo, customers, agents, finance, insurance, technology or advisory assignments toward connected parties.
 



  





**The first 120 days** 




  





 The Director will trace representative high\-risk and high\-value shipments; reconcile client\-money accounts and advances; review customs, sanctions and conduct incidents; test customer and agent concentration on collected contribution; examine recent acquisitions or branches with overdue controls; and establish direct access to compliance, internal audit and whistle\-blower channels.
 



 Within one year, the Board expects clearer principal\-agent boundaries, protected client money, stronger trade screening, realistic shipment profitability, controlled overseas agents and faster closure of customs, claims and receivable exposures.

**About The Role**
 Zeta is seeking a Associate Director – Legal to serve as a strategic advisor within its legal team, supporting the company’s banking, payments, and technology business as it scales across India, the US, the UK, and other global markets.
   

  

 This is a high\-impact, product\-facing role for a seasoned banking and finance lawyer who can operate at the intersection of financial services regulation and cutting\-edge technology, ensuring Zeta’s products, partnerships, and client programs are designed and delivered in a manner that is legally sound and regulator\-ready. Reporting into Zeta’s India legal leadership and partnering closely with Product, Compliance, and Risk teams, the role carries significant autonomy and visibility — requiring an individual who can independently own matters end to end, negotiate directly with banks, NBFCs, and technology partners, run and manage a team of capable lawyers, and help shape the legal function of a fast\-growing, high\-growth fintech at the core of India’s digital banking transformation.
   

  

**Responsibilities**
**Product and platform legal support**
* Deliver day\-to\-day legal counsel across Zeta’s banking technology stack, covering card issuance, transaction processing, lending and loan management, core account and ledger functionality, and Digital Credit\-as\-a\-Service and Credit Line on UPI (CLOU), BNPL, and EMI\-conversion products.
* Advise product and engineering teams on the regulatory implications of platform features, including card management, real\-time authorization and settlement, digital lending, account lifecycle management, instrument lifecycle management (physical and virtual cards, tokens, and QR), transaction switching, and fraud and dispute management.


**Contract drafting, review, and negotiation**
* Draft, review, and negotiate agreements with banks, financial institutions, card networks, and technology partners, including platform licensing, SaaS and managed\-services arrangements, program\-management agreements, and BIN or balance\-sheet sponsorship deals underpinning Banking\-as\-a\-Service and embedded banking offerings.
* Structure co\-brand, affinity, and fintech partnership arrangements, and draft and negotiate credit card, debit card, prepaid instrument, and co\-branded card program agreements spanning retail, commercial, private\-label, and secured card products.
* Structure and paper credit lines, BNPL, and loan\-installment features and related payment and settlement arrangements, and negotiate digital lending, co\-lending, and lending service provider (LSP) agreements.
* Draft, negotiate, and manage fintech partnership, third\-party vendor, and platform licensing agreements, allocating responsibility, liability, and data\-handling obligations across Zeta, its clients, and its partners.


**Regulatory advisory**
* Advise on RBI guidelines including the Digital Lending Directions, Credit Card and Debit Card Issuance and Conduct Directions, and Master Direction on Outsourcing of IT Services; NPCI regulations governing UPI and RuPay; and PPI rules under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act — tracking evolving developments and assessing their impact on Zeta’s products and programs.
* Advise on card\-network rules, grievance redressal frameworks, and partner bank agreement requirements for card and payments programs.
* Advise on data privacy, cybersecurity, and data\-localization requirements under the DPDP Act and IT Act, and on legal considerations relevant to maintaining SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications.
* Provide legal input on regulatory filings, regulator queries and inspections, and legal risk assessments for new products and partnerships, and support the development of internal legal playbooks and templates.


**Broader legal support**
* While anchored in banking and finance law, comfortable providing practical legal support across other areas as they arise for a fast\-growing technology business, including corporate, commercial, employment, and technology or intellectual property matters.


**Skills**
* Regulatory and commercial acumen: Commercially minded, pragmatic; translates complex regulation into clear, actionable guidance for non\-legal stakeholders.
* Stakeholder management and communication: Strong communication and negotiation skills, sound and independent judgment, ability to counsel senior management strategically.
* Execution and prioritization: Highly organized and detail\-oriented; manages multiple matters simultaneously in a fast\-paced, high\-growth setting; ability to leverage AI for legal work highly preferred.
* Team leadership and people management: Ability to lead and manage a team effectively.
* Ownership and adaptability: Proactive self\-starter, energized by ambiguity, comfortable in unfamiliar areas of law, takes ownership of outcomes, thrives in a collaborative, product\-driven culture at the frontier of banking and fintech.


**Experience And Qualification**
* LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognized institution; qualified to practice law in India. LLM is a plus.
* 9–12 years of post\-qualification experience as a banking and finance lawyer, gained in a top tier law firm.
* H ands\-on expertise across digital lending, credit and debit cards, prepaid and co\-branded card programs, payments, and fintech regulation.
* Contract drafting \& negotiation: Strong contract drafting, review, and negotiation skills across commercial, technology, and financial\-services agreements.
* Working command of RBI, NPCI, and PPI frameworks.
* Experience advising on software license, SaaS, IT services, and IP licensing matters; f amiliarity with Banking\-as\-a\-Service; c ross\-border regulatory exposure.
* Proven experience leading and managing a team, including handling administrative responsibilities alongside substantive legal work.

title: Head - Legal & Compliance
description:
Head — Legal \& Compliance \| Vantrock Real Assets Private Limited \| Mumbai Metropolitan Region
 



  
 



 Not a general counsel with a department, and not a land\-law seat. One qualified lawyer who commands outside counsel, runs the secretarial calendar for every entity through a small team, and holds the compliance line — for a real assets platform forming a dozen entities and building fast.
 



  
 



 A note before you read on. The team structure, reporting lines, direct reports, seat titles and hiring entity described in this brief reflect the platform's current plan and may change as the platform builds out. Compensation and incentive structures are confirmed in the offer, not here.
 



  
 



 REPORTS TO: Chief Financial Officer · EXPERIENCE: 8–14 years as a qualified lawyer, a meaningful part of it in\-house at a real estate or real\-assets business
 



  
 



 ABOUT VANTROCK
 



 Vantrock is India's independent, operator\-led real assets platform — real assets only — with logistics and industrial as the first phase of its growth.
 



 Founded by Anshul Singhal, Founder \& CEO — three institutional platforms built from zero, the fourth on his own capital; 52 million sq ft delivered (32 million as developer, 20 million as contractor) across his three prior platforms.
 



  
 



 THE FINANCE \& ACCOUNTS TEAM
 



 Vantrock keeps its books in\-house. The finance function owns every number from the site to the board.
 



 Twenty\-one seats when fully built; sixteen live now, one of them already filled. Small enough that every person in it is known by name to the founder; large enough to run a platform properly. Every seat in the team is a builder's seat: the function does not exist yet in the form described here, and the people who join it now are the ones who will decide what it becomes.
 



  
 



 JUDGMENT IN\-HOUSE, DRAFTING OUTSIDE
 



 Vantrock does not run a legal department in the conventional sense, and it does not intend to. Formal opinions come from external firms. Transaction documents are drafted by the counsel retained for the transaction. Litigation, where it arises, is run by litigators. What the platform keeps in\-house is the one thing that cannot be bought by the hour: the person who knows the business well enough to decide what to ask, whom to ask, when the answer is wrong, and when to say no.
 



  
 



 WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
 



 A platform forming a dozen entities, signing construction contracts, taking on lenders, bringing in institutional co\-investors and preparing a fund vehicle generates a volume of legal and secretarial work that cannot be run out of the founder's inbox and a handful of law firms' engagement letters. Today it is. The question of who owns the contract before it goes to counsel, who tracks the ROC calendar across a dozen entities, who tells the founder that a clause he has agreed in principle is a problem — has no answer inside the building.
 



  
 



 WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 



 1\. Corporate legal, commanded. Every contract, transaction, structure and dispute scoped by you before counsel is engaged, briefed by you, reviewed by you before it is signed — and the internal view formed first, so that outside counsel is answering the right question.
 



 2\. The empanelled firms. Choose them, brief them, hold them to fee and quality, and know which firm to use for what.
 



 3\. The secretarial calendar for every entity. Board and partner meetings, resolutions, statutory registers, ROC and LLP filings, annual compliance — for the development company, the investment manager, the sponsor vehicles and every project entity.
 



 4\. The compliance line. A single register of what the group must do, by when, under which law or contract — statutory, regulatory, investor undertakings, with lender covenants mirrored from the corporate finance team's calendar — with an owner and a status against every line, reviewed monthly with the CFO.
 



 5\. Construction and commercial contracts. The platform's standard forms — contractor, consultant, project\-management, lease, facility\-management — built once with counsel and then held, so that the tenth contract is negotiated from the platform's paper, not the counterparty's.
 



 6\. The boundary with land. Working with the investments team's land lawyer so that every land transaction hands over cleanly into an entity, a contract and a filing calendar — with nothing dropped between the two seats.
 



 7\. The team. Recruit, direct and develop the company secretary, the CS\-intermediate and the paralegal; add the second paralegal when volume demands it; and build a seat that a Chief Compliance Officer can be added alongside without a turf line.
 



  
 



 WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
 



 ESSENTIAL
 



 – A qualified lawyer, enrolled with a Bar Council, with 8–14 years in practice — of which a meaningful part in\-house at a real estate developer, an institutional platform, or a business of comparable entity count and contract volume.
 



 – Corporate and commercial law as your core: contracts, entity formation and governance, transactions, employment, the Companies Act and the LLP Act in daily use.
 



 – Having commanded external law firms as the client — scoping, briefing, reviewing, pushing back on the advice and the bill — rather than as the associate drafting for them.
 



 – Company\-secretarial practice understood well enough to supervise it: you know what a filing calendar for a multi\-entity group looks like and what breaks when it slips, even if you have never filed a form yourself.
 



 – Comfortable telling a founder no, in writing, with the reason — and being right often enough to be listened to.
 



 – Based in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, or relocating before joining.
 



 WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT
 



 – Not a general counsel's seat with a large department beneath. The team is a company secretary, a CS\-intermediate and a paralegal. The judgment is yours; the drafting is bought.
 



 – Not a land\-law seat. Title, land acquisition and land litigation belong to the investments team's land lawyer. If land is your first love, that is the seat to look for.
 



  
 



 HOW YOU WILL WORK
 



 – Judgment in\-house, drafting outside. You form the view, then engage counsel; you never engage counsel to form the view.
 



 – Everything runs on the platform's dashboards. The compliance register, the secretarial calendar, the contract library and the panel\-firm scorecard live on the operating layer, not in a private folder.
 



  
 



 COMPENSATION
 



 Vantrock benchmarks compensation against the upper quartile for the role and market, weighted toward equity for candidates who want to build with us long\-term. We discuss specific numbers in the first conversation rather than anchoring either side prematurely.
 



  
 



 CULTURAL FIT
 



 We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co\-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
 



 AI proficiency is a standing requirement in every Vantrock seat. You work fluently with AI tools for research, modelling, drafting and analysis, and you build on the platform's dashboards rather than around them. A supervised AI Proficiency Test is part of the process for every seat, at every level of seniority, and we say so openly.
 



 Partner command is the second standing requirement. The books are ours, but auditors, banks, the fund administrator, valuers, law firms and system vendors are commanded by this team — briefed, held to a standard, integrated — never deferred to. We hire for judgment and accountability.
 



  
 



 HOW WE WILL ASSESS
 



 Everyone who applies hears from us within two working days. It carries two links: a fixed set of six questions answered by AI interview — about forty minutes, and the first work sample; we review it before the CV — and the Vantrock AI Proficiency Test, which every hire takes at every level. From there:
 



 1\. The Matter conversation. The matters on your sheet: the one where you overruled outside counsel and were right, the one where you were wrong, and how you built a compliance register the first time. With the CFO — or, until that seat is filled, the Founder \& CEO.
 



 2\. A 90\-minute supervised case. A contractor's standard\-form construction contract with planted problems, and a two\-page group structure — from which you produce the issues note you would send to counsel, the three clauses you would refuse, and the filing calendar the structure implies. Defended to the Founder \& CEO and the CFO once in seat.
 



 Once we have received your application, your AI interview and your test, we will reach out with next steps. Your application is confidential: it is seen only by the Founder's Office and the hiring lead, and nothing is shared with your current employer or referenced without your consent.
 



  
 



 TO APPLY
 



 Write to careers@vantrock.com with the subject line "Head — Legal \& Compliance — \[your name]", and attach:
 



 – Your CV. This is mandatory — a LinkedIn profile alone is not an application; we will read your LinkedIn as well.
 



 – Your Matter Sheet — one row per matter or transaction you led in\-house: type, entities involved, counsel commanded, value or stake in ₹ crore where relevant, year, outcome, your role. The template is available on request. Every row will be discussed.
 



 – Your notice period and what you would need to see to move.
 



 – One short paragraph: the clause that most often gets past a founder in a construction contract, and how you would make sure it never gets past this one. That paragraph matters more than the CV.
 



 We read everything that arrives with a Matter Sheet and a paragraph — properly, not skimmed. If this sounds like your seat, write to us.
 



  
 



 We don't hire roles. We build the platform. · Ownership, not employment. · Builders hire builders.
 




 Founder \& CEO, Vantrock

description:
Counsel — Land \& Transaction Risk \| Vantrock Real Assets Private Limited \| Mumbai Metropolitan Region
 



  
 



 Not a law\-firm seat and not a compliance seat. Every asset this platform buys starts as land, and the founder's own capital goes in first – so title, tenure and approval risk sit with us, not with an investor. This seat controls that risk: it commissions the country's best firms, holds them to the standard and the date, and turns what comes back into a decision.
 



  
 



 ABOUT VANTROCK
 



 Vantrock is an independent real assets platform. Real assets only. We start where we know the ground: logistics, warehousing and industrial parks, across the full chain – first mile, last mile, city\-centre, dark\-store and self\-storage formats, and logistics\-anchored mixed\-use developments with distribution below and office above. From there, in sequence and only as each is delivered: industrial plots; suburban campuses, GCC and back\-office space; strata offices; and, in parallel, data centres and senior living.
 



  
 



 Two decades on this ground and a gap institutional capital left open below the 100\-acre logistics park. The first phase: 10\-to\-50\-acre parcels taken through approvals quickly on the founder's own capital and turned into 2\.5 lakh to 1\.2 million sq ft campuses – shovel\-ready before an investor is ever asked to commit. Pipeline 10 million sq ft; ground breaks on the first 2 million sq ft in January 2027\.
 



  
 



 Three parts, kept deliberately separate. The founder's own balance sheet takes the first risk. Vantrock Real Assets Private Limited – the employer for this seat – is the development manager and operator, with its own board, team and governance. Vantrock Investment Managers LLP is the investment manager; its team underwrites every asset independently and answers to an independent Investment Committee. Assets enter a strategy at cost, with no founder premium, and the platform earns only after its investors have.
 



  
 



 Vantrock was founded by Anshul Singhal, Founder \& CEO, who has built three institutional platforms from zero and is building the fourth on his own capital. 52 million sq ft delivered (32 million as developer, 20 million as contractor), over 2,000 acres acquired, all litigation\-free, more than 200 buildings, and two SEBI Category II funds run to a successful close. Delivered across the founder's three prior platforms. We don't hire roles. We build the platform.
 



  
 



 THE LAND \& INVESTMENTS TEAM
 



 The Land \& Investments team originates, underwrites, structures and closes the land and platform transactions the pipeline is built from, and stays with each asset for its life. The legal function inside it is deliberately two people – a Counsel and a Paralegal. It controls land risk and turnaround across a national pipeline rather than doing the volume work: the country's best land practices do that, and the Big Four advisers do the tax. Judgment, standards, dates and the file stay in\-house.
 



  
 



 THE SEAT
 



 Reports to: Chief Investment Officer / Head of Land \& Investments. Dotted line to the Chief Financial Officer.
 



 Direct reports: Paralegal — Land \& Documentation
 



 Location: Mumbai Metropolitan Region — in person. Substantial travel to NCR, Pune, Bengaluru and to sites, sub\-registrar offices and revenue records wherever a deal sits.
 



 Experience: At least 5 years of relevant land and real estate property law. Total years matter less than those five.
 



  
 



 Team structure, reporting lines, direct reports, seat titles and the hiring entity described here reflect the current plan and may change as the platform builds out. Compensation is confirmed in the offer.
 



  
 



 WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS
 



 Every asset this platform buys starts as land, and every land deal carries a legal risk that either gets found before signing or gets paid for afterwards. The founder's own capital goes in first, before any investor is asked to commit, which means title, tenure, encumbrance and approval risk are absorbed by the house and not passed on. This seat is where that risk is controlled.
 



  
 



 The Counsel is not the person who writes the opinion – the country's best land practices do that, and will keep doing it. This seat commissions them, structures the question, holds them to the standard and the date, and translates what comes back into price, structure and whether we proceed. Nobody knows every state's land law and we are not looking for someone who claims to: the record changes name and shape at every border – 7/12 and mutation entries in Maharashtra, Record of Rights and pahani in Karnataka, chitta, adangal and patta in Tamil Nadu, khasra and jamabandi in the north – and what we need is someone who can land in a new state, work out what the record proves, instruct the right counsel and come back with an answer. Resourceful, street\-smart, solution\-minded; the answer is rarely in a textbook.
 



  
 



 WHAT YOU WILL OWN
 



 1\. Own land risk on every live transaction.
 



 2\. Command the firms.
 



 3\. Own the turnaround clock.
 



 4\. Build and hold the gold standard.
 



 5\. Own stamp duty, registration and the tax read.
 



 6\. Read the paper record for what it actually says.
 



 7\. Structure and paper the transaction, then close it.
 



  
 



 TRAVEL IS A REAL AND CENTRAL PART OF THIS SEAT
 



 Not an occasional site visit. Expect to be out of Mumbai a meaningful part of every month, in the states where our deals sit: at the parcel, in revenue and sub\-registrar offices, in local counsel's chambers, and across the table from landowners and their lawyers. Records in India are not fully digital and the risks that matter are rarely the ones already written into a report. If travelling to a tehsil office in a state whose language you do not speak sounds like the wrong kind of work, this is not your seat.
 



  
 



 WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
 



 – At least five years of relevant land and real estate property law. Total years of experience are not the filter; those five are.
 



 – LL.B. from a recognised university, and enrolment with a State Bar Council.
 



 – Hands\-on title diligence on land: chain of title, revenue records, encumbrance, tenure and conversion, litigation search — on deals you personally worked, not supervised from a distance.
 



 – Drafting and negotiating real estate transaction documents: sale deeds, development and joint development agreements, leases and lease deeds, agreements to sell, powers of attorney, conditions precedent and closing documents.
 



 – Experience instructing and managing external counsel — scoping the work, reviewing it, and pushing back when it does not answer the question.
 



 – Working knowledge of land\-related statutes and the approval path for developing land in at least one Indian state — the local record and its vocabulary, tenancy and ceiling history, conversion and land use — and the appetite to learn the next state quickly, on the job.
 



  
 



 What this role is not
 



 – Not a general corporate or compliance seat. Company law, securities and fund compliance sit elsewhere in the group; this seat is land and the transactions built on it.
 



 – Not a litigation seat. Disputes are handled by counsel; you assess what a dispute does to a deal.
 



  
 



 COMPENSATION
 



 Vantrock benchmarks compensation against the upper quartile for the role and market, weighted toward equity for candidates who want to build with us long\-term. We discuss specific numbers in the first conversation rather than anchoring either side prematurely. Wealth creation is part of the engine, not only the salary: performance\-linked bonuses and ESOP\-linked incentives, priced to the seat and confirmed in the offer.
 



  
 



 CULTURAL FIT
 



 We're building Vantrock over a decade, not a funding cycle. We're looking for people who treat technology as the default answer rather than a supplement, who want to be co\-builders of the platform rather than employees executing instructions, and who are comfortable saying "I don't know" and "I was wrong." If you want a defined role with defined edges, this isn't the right seat. If you want to help build an institution from zero, it might be.
 



  
 



 AI proficiency and partner command are standing requirements in every Vantrock seat: you work fluently with AI tools and build on the platform's systems, and you command the institutional partners who execute the transactional work. A supervised AI Proficiency Test is part of the process for every seat, at every level.
 



  
 



 HOW WE WILL ASSESS
 



 One email within two working days of applying, with two links: six fixed questions answered by AI interview – about forty minutes, the first work sample, reviewed before the CV – and the Vantrock AI Proficiency Test. Then: The Land Deal Sheet conversation; A 90\-minute case; Case defence with the Chief Investment Officer / Head of Land \& Investments and the Chief Financial Officer; References. Once we have your application, interview and test, we reach out with next steps. Your application is confidential – seen only by the Founder's Office and the hiring lead, and nothing is shared with your current employer.
 



  
 



 TO APPLY
 



 Write to careers@vantrock.com with the subject line "Counsel — Land \& Transaction Risk — \[your name]", and attach:
 



 – Your CV. This is mandatory — a LinkedIn profile alone is not an application; we will read your LinkedIn as well.
 



 – Your Land Deal Sheet — one row per transaction you have worked on: state and micro\-market, parcel size, transaction type, your role, year, and the principal legal issue you resolved. A simple table is fine; every row will be discussed.
 



 – Your notice period and what you would need to see to move.
 



 – One short paragraph: the single title or tenure issue you would check first on a 30\-acre industrial parcel in a state you have never worked in, and why that one. That paragraph matters more than the CV.
 



  
 



 We read everything that arrives with a Deal Sheet and a paragraph — properly, not skimmed. If this sounds like your seat, write to us.
 



  
 



 We don't hire roles. We build the platform. · Ownership, not employment. · Builders hire builders.
 



  
 



 Founder \& CEO, Vantrock

description:
**Company Profile**
 Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 41 countries.
   

  

 From the largest global institutions to innovative new hedge funds, investors come to Morgan Stanley for sales, trading, and market\-making services in almost every type of financial instruments including stocks, bonds, derivatives, foreign exchange, and commodities. Our professionals provide liquidity and content to clients around the world, actively assessing and managing risk, trading securities, and planning and executing transactions in the fast\-changing markets. As the needs of our clients become increasingly complex, we often develop customized solutions.
   

  

 As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career \- a place for people to learn, to achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture.
   

  

**Department Profile**
 The Fixed Income Division is comprised of Interest Rate and Foreign Exchange Products, Credit Products, and Commodity Products and Distribution. Professionals in the Division assess and actively manages risk, trade securities, and structure as well as execute innovative transactions in the fast\-paced and constantly changing global markets. The Commodities business is a market leader across a broad range of commodities markets, with expertise in areas including client risk management, financing solutions and investor products Sales \& Trading
   

  

 From the largest global institutions to innovative new hedge funds, investors come to Morgan Stanley for sales, trading, and market\-making services in almost every type of financial instruments including stocks, bonds, derivatives, foreign exchange, and commodities. Our professionals provide liquidity and content to clients around the world, actively assessing and managing risk, trading securities, and planning and executing transactions in the fast\-changing markets. As the needs of our clients become increasingly complex, we often develop customized solutions.
   

  

**Background on the Team**
 The Institutional Securities Documentation (“ISD”) team sits within FID’s Business Control Unit (“BCU”) and is a first line team comprised of Non\-Market Risk (Operational Risk), Counterparty Risk, Conduct Risk and Contract Negotiations. The ISD Team covers the contract negotiation function for trading agreements for FID.
   

  

 The FID ISD team is currently looking for a derivatives and financing documentation negotiator. The role will involve daily interaction and collaboration with Sales \& Trading, Risk Management, Credit Risk, Legal, Operations and myriad other ISG stakeholders, as well as daily and direct engagement with clients and their counsel.
   

  

 ISD is a global team based in several locations (including New York, London, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Mumbai Budapest and Singapore) and the broader Mumbai ISD team works closely with each of the regional teams supporting the Fixed Income Division in the Americas, EMEA and Asia\-Pacific. We are looking for an individual to join the Mumbai ISD team supporting the Americas or EMEA region.
   

  

**Primary Responsibilities**
* Drafting and negotiating legal documentation (including master agreements, amendments and ancillary documents \- CDEAs, DRAs etc) required for OTC derivatives, repurchase or stock loan transactions.
* Handling client negotiations and any related projects to ensure timely execution and completion.
* Review and analyse legal documentation to determine capacity and authority to enter into OTC derivatives transactions, repurchase or stock loan transactions.
* Identifying necessary documentation for the clients to trade securities or OTC derivatives and perform related due diligence scans.
* Actively participate in global team projects on initiatives such as risk management, regulatory\-driven projects, etc. and ensuring timely execution and completion.
* Liaise with clients, business units, external legal counsel, risk management and other infrastructure groups within the firm (e.g. Operations, Tax, Credit, etc) throughout the negotiation process, including analyzing and presenting negotiation issues to relevant stakeholders.
* Understanding and adhering to established procedures.
* Communicating with clients and external counsel.
* Update internal systems regarding negotiation status, documentation database, project trackers, etc.
* Handle post\-negotiation matters including arranging for signing, coordinating the filing of electronic documents and original documents, dispatching documents to counterparties, etc.
* Provide mentoring, training and coaching for junior team members
* Responding to queries on the master documentation from various departments including business functions


**Skills Required**
* Law graduate with experience/knowledge in the ISDA Master Agreement and/or other derivatives documentation.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and manage teams effectively, ensuring alignment with organisational goals while fostering professional growth.
* International work experience is preferred.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills; be prepared to speak to clients (internal and external) at all times.
* Proficiency in English is a must.
* Good team player.
* Solid quantitative skills and strong interest in business, economics and law.
* Willingness and ability to provide quality service to the Firm's clients and to promote and enhance the Morgan Stanley franchise.
* Willingness to work in dynamic environment and the ability to excel under pressure.
* Proficiency and interest in technology and systems development.
* Essential Characteristics: Organized, pro\-active, ability to multi\-task and work efficiently, detail\-oriented and self\-sufficient.
* GMRA or GMSLA negotiation experience would be useful, but not essential.


**What You Can Expect From Morgan Stanley**
 At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values \- putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back \- aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work\-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.
   

  

 To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about\-us/global\-offices into your browser.
   

  

 Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.
   

  

 Our workforce reflects a broad cross\-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences.
   

  

 For more information, please visit: https://www.morganstanley.com/people\-opportunities/eeo.

 AlphaGrep IM is the brainchild of the team at AlphaGrep, a SEBI\-regulated broker and multi\-asset proprietary trading firm focused on quantitative trading across more than 20 global exchanges.
   

  

 We are looking for a bright and resourceful individual to join our
 **Compliance team in Mumbai** 
 .
   

  

 Role

 Compliance

 Key Responsibilities

* Coordinate and ensure timely submission of regulatory returns and filings applicable to AIF, PMS and Investment Advisory businesses.
* Review regulatory submissions for accuracy, completeness and consistency.
* Coordinate with Operations, Finance, Fund Accounting, Legal and other teams for information required for regulatory reporting.
